**Bottom line:** The claim is false as literally worded. Treating ">85% round-trip efficiency" as covering the *full* electricity→heat→electricity loop conflates it with two different, much easier metrics (charging efficiency and heat-retention efficiency, both legitimately >85-95%). The actual discharge stage (heat→electricity) requires a heat engine that is Carnot-limited to ~59-64% even in an idealized, lossless, zero-power limit at 290-565°C against an ambient heat sink — and real small-scale (≈1-2 MWe) hardware at 5 MWh realistically delivers a full round-trip efficiency around 18-34% (central ≈26%). On cost, the same 5 MWh system is roughly 2-12× (central ≈6×) more expensive per kWh of deliverable electric energy than a same-energy lithium-ion BESS, because the cheap storage media is swamped by a disproportionately expensive, small-scale power-conversion stage. Overall confidence: MEDIUM (the qualitative verdict is robust across all tested ranges; the exact multipliers carry residual uncertainty from several `?`-marked inputs, including one source — the NREL ATB page — this run could not reach due to a DNS failure).
